research_question: What is the effect of collaborative care, compared with usual or standard care, on mental-health-related quality of life at up to 6 months in adults with severe mental illness living in the community?
outcome_description: Endpoint mental-health-related quality of life score at up to 6 months measured by validated quality-of-life instruments (e.g., SF-12/SF-36 Mental Component Summary, WHOQOL-BREF psychological domain)
positive_direction: Higher mental-health-related quality of life favoring collaborative care
search_queries: collaborative care severe mental illness quality of life trial
collaborative care schizophrenia bipolar randomized controlled trial
integrated care severe mental illness mental health quality of life outcome
inclusion_criteria: Empirical studies evaluating collaborative care models versus usual or standard care in community-dwelling adults with severe mental illness
Studies reporting quantitative mental-health-related quality of life outcomes at follow-up of up to 6 months using validated assessment scales
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, protocol papers, or theoretical papers)
No comparison between collaborative care and a standard/usual care control condition
No quantitative outcome data reporting mental-health-related quality of life at up to 6 months (means and SDs, SEs, or equivalent effect size data)
Unrelated to adults with severe mental illness (e.g., schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, schizoaffective disorder) living in the community
moderators_to_extract: Specific psychiatric diagnosis / severe mental illness profile
Quality of life measurement instrument (e.g., SF-12 MCS, WHOQOL-BREF psychological domain)
Assessment timepoint (weeks or months, up to 6 months)
Collaborative care intervention components (e.g., care manager background, liaison frequency)
